clues: This city is the capital of a region in the north of Spain. It sits on flat land by a river that flows to a much bigger river.
This inland city is harsher than the wet coast near it. Its winters bite with more cold, its summers burn with more heat, and its summers stay dry.
This city was set up by a Roman chief named Pompey in about 75 BC. He built it while his men fought a war in Spain.
Ernest Hemingway put this city in a famed novel in 1926. The book was about the city and its big summer fair in July.
Each July, bulls run fast through the streets of this city in a famed fair. Brave crowds run in front of them for nine wild days.
